questions.q: How does the formation of shadows show that light travels in a straight line?
answer: Light travels in a straight line, and shadows are clear evidence of this.

answer.text: A shadow forms when an opaque object comes in the path of light and blocks it. Three things are needed: a source of light, an opaque object, and a screen on which the shadow falls.

Because light cannot bend around the object, the region behind it receives no light and appears dark. The shadow always takes the outline, or shape, of the object, not its colour, and its size changes with the object's distance from the source and screen.
A pinhole camera forms an inverted image of an object for the same reason — light travels straight through the tiny hole.

questions.q: Describe the image formed by a plane mirror and explain lateral inversion.
answer: Reflection is the bouncing back of light from a shiny surface, and a plane mirror forms a clear image by reflection.

answer.text: The image in a plane mirror is virtual, meaning it cannot be caught on a screen; it is erect, or the same way up; it is the same size as the object; and it appears as far behind the mirror as the object is in front of it.

The image is also laterally inverted, which means the left and right sides are exchanged — your right hand appears as the left hand of your image. This is why the word AMBULANCE is written in reverse on the front of the vehicle, so that it reads correctly in the mirror of the vehicle ahead.
